newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA'S PRAIRIES MAY SEE UP TO AN INCH OF RAIN-EC.
newsitem.headline: CANADA'S PRAIRIES MAY SEE UP TO AN INCH OF RAIN-EC.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Wednesday were forecast to receive up to one inch of rain in the next three days before dry weather returns, an Environment Canada meteorologist said.
"A low pressure trough enters Alberta Thursday evening, bringing extensive precipitation to the central parts, 20 to 25 mm (1.0 inch) around Edmonton," meteorologist Andre Pelland said.
The system was forecast to weaken entering Saskatchewan Friday as scattered showers were expected to drop 15 mm (0.6 inch) of rain around and north of Saskatoon, Pelland said.
Saskatchewan's southern grainbelt should remain dry.

A ban on campfires was extended Wednesday to the Cypress Hills Provincial Park in the southwest after similar bans were imposed in the central and western areas, Saskatchewan Environment and Resource Management Minister Lorne Scott said.
Scattered light showers were expected to reach western Manitoba by Friday evening and Winnipeg by Saturday afternoon, Pelland said.
Cooler temperatures in the low to mid-20s Celsius were expected to follow the low pressure trough through the weekend and early into next week across the Prairies, he added.
A high pressure ridge on Sunday was expected to bring drier conditions to the region, Pelland said.
